standard_prerequisites.name: Bounded progressive colourings, the halting set and its modulus
standard_prerequisites.statement: A colouring into finite sets of natural numbers is progressive when every nonempty value has least element at least the least element of its argument, and it is constrained by a bounding function when the size of each value is bounded by that function at the least element of the argument; the halting set is the first Turing jump of the empty set and it is equivalent to a total function, its modulus, in the sense that a function dominating that modulus computes the halting set. The author's own notation is retained inside the counted statement and proof.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted proposition is the tightness half of the article's main theorem: it exhibits a barrier whose defining colouring is computable from the halting set and whose free sets recover the halting set, so the avoidance result for computable barriers cannot be extended to this one.

core_obligations: Choose the bounding function to be the modulus of the halting set, which is itself computable from the halting set, and define the colouring on a number x to be the interval of integers from x plus one up to that modulus value (source lines 1266-1267).
Observe that the colouring is progressive and constrained by the chosen bounding function, so that it is an admissible instance of the principle whose tightness is at stake (source line 1267).

Conclude for free sets: if H is an infinite set free for that colouring and x is smaller than y in H, then y must exceed the modulus value at x, because otherwise the interval of the colouring at x would meet H and the value at x would be a forbidden colour; so an increasing enumeration of H majorises the modulus and therefore computes the halting set (source line 1268).

proof_roadmap.step: Take the modulus of the halting set as the bounding function and the interval up to that value as the colouring.
Note that the colouring is progressive and constrained.
For a free set, consecutive elements majorise the modulus, so the set computes the halting set.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2412.11598v3 的**无 label** Proposition（源 1262-1264 行，证明 1265-1269 行）：存在 ∅′-可计算的函数 b 与 b-constrained 的 progressive 着色 f，使每个无穷 f-free 集都计算 ∅′。关键操作不是例行核验：要先把 b 取成 ∅′ 的模数、把 f(x) 定义成区间 [x+1,…,b(x)]（1266-1267 行），再验证 f 既 progressive 又 b-constrained（1267 行），最后用「free 集里 x<y 必推出 y>b(x)」这一条把 H 的递增枚举变成**支配 b 的函数**，从而 H ≥_T ∅′（1268 行）。难点在于把「free」这一禁止条件翻译成对元素间距的支配性估计——这正是与主定理（可计算 barrier 的锥回避）形成紧致的对照；原文位置在证明的 1266-1267、1267、1268 行。

editorial_notes: The counted unit is the article's own unlabelled Proposition at source lines 1262-1264 together with its proof at source lines 1265-1269, a straight adjacent pairing in the pinned file. It is the proposition the article states immediately after its main theorem on strong cone avoidance, and the surrounding prose presents it as the tightness of that theorem. The pinned file is the article's fixed version arXiv:2412.11598v3 under CC BY 4.0.

This statement carries no source label, so the lane identifiers it by its opening line: the claim key is the article's identifier with the addition of the statement's first line, and the statement span is the complete proposition environment from its opening marker to its closing marker. The same convention the project applies to unlabelled statements elsewhere.

Because the statement has no label, the shared gate refuses the interval by design, so the lane ran its documented substitute checks instead: the live occupancy index reports the interval free, no card of any lane carries a token derived from the statement, and the public index carries exactly one entry for this source, at lines 585-587, which does not overlap this interval. The substitution and its outcome are recorded in the card's dedup block and in the lane STATUS.

The retained statement and proof contain no reference to another labelled result and no citation, so this card carries no navigation pointer and no bibliography entry. The notions it uses, the modulus of the halting set and the defining properties of a bounded progressive colouring, are recorded in the standard prerequisites; both are introduced earlier in the article.
